title: TriageDecision
description: Triage decision: the ready_to_build, clarification_questions, derived_user_request, confidence, and rationale fields below. Place these fields directly as the tool input — no outer wrapper.

ready_to_build.description: True when the issue and comments identify the requested behaviour, target surface, and expected result clearly enough for downstream discovery to create user stories without guessing. False when important behaviour, scope, data shape, user-visible outcome, or priority is still ambiguous. Must be false whenever clarification_questions is non-empty.

clarification_questions.description: 1-3 sharp clarification questions, each answerable by the issue author, whose answers would change what gets built. Empty when ready_to_build is true. Posted publicly on the GitHub issue, so keep them concise and avoid surfacing internal model uncertainty. Do not ask the author to choose internal class names, file paths, libraries, or implementation details — those are downstream decisions.

derived_user_request.description: Concise, implementation-ready restatement of the issue, including resolved constraints and acceptance details from comments. Required when ready_to_build is true; empty string otherwise. When non-empty, format as compact GitHub-flavored Markdown instead of a single plain sentence: start with a bold label such as `**Request:**`, then add short bullets for acceptance details, constraints, or explicitly unchanged behaviour when those details exist. Preserve the user's meaning; do not invent requirements, implementation steps, headings, or file paths just to make the Markdown fuller.

confidence.description: Self-assessed confidence in the readiness decision. Use 'low' when the inputs are mostly inferred, 'medium' when comments resolve the main ambiguities, and 'high' when the issue and comments specify behaviour, surface, and outcome explicitly.

rationale.description: Brief justification for the triage decision. Posted to the workflow trace for human reviewers. Format as compact GitHub-flavored Markdown rather than a single plain line: use 2-3 short bullets or bold labels such as `**Decision:**`, `**Evidence:**`, and `**Open risk:**` when helpful. Keep the same reasoning content as a normal rationale; do not add speculation or repeat the full derived request.
